title: Declarative Ingestion for the Operational Lakehouse

slides.title: Declarative Ingestion for the Operational Lakehouse
slides.subtitle: A config-driven bronze and silver framework on Lakeflow Spark Declarative Pipelines
slides.author: Databricks

slides.title: From hand-built tables to declared pipelines
left: Silver tables built and maintained table by table
No common contract for schema, keys or quality
Cadence and scope differ per environment by hand
Hard to trace a table back to the code behind it
right: New bronze catalog owned end to end by the framework
Silver declared by pipelines, replacing the legacy tables
One data contract per table, enforced in CI
Every table tagged to its pipeline, config and code
slides.notes: The change is ownership: nothing lands in bronze or silver unless configuration declares it, and the framework detects anything that does.
slides.subtitle: Ownership of bronze and silver moves from people to configuration

slides.title: Architecture: Qlik files to governed silver
bullets: Qlik Replicate lands full-load and change files per table
Auto Loader picks them up through file events, never listing
Bronze: append-only history with every Qlik header kept
Silver: AUTO CDC on contract keys, SCD1 or SCD2 per table
Ops schema: event logs, table registry, audits
slides.card_content:
Qlik Replicate
  <group>/<TABLE>/      full load
  <group>/<TABLE>__ct/  changes
        |  file events
        v
bronze_<env>.facets.<table>
  history, contract schema
        |  drop before-images
        |  contract expectations
        v  AUTO CDC
silver_<env>.facets.<table>
  current state / history
slides.notes: Bronze is the system of record and is never reset in prod. A Qlik table reload rebuilds only that table's silver from bronze using a recorded cutoff.
slides.subtitle: Event-driven, contract-governed, one generic pipeline per group

slides.title: Onboarding is configuration, not code
slides.subtitle: ~2,700 source tables become ~20 pipelines with zero per-table pipeline code

items: table.yml: a few lines of ops config
Scaffolded from a data dictionary or Qlik .dfm
Up to 150 tables, one Qlik task folder
One generic SDP entrypoint for every group
Event log, notifications and tags included
dev / tst: weekly run over 1 day of changes
sandbox: on file arrival, synthetic Qlik data

slides.notes: Weekly rather than monthly in dev/tst: the file-events cache expires after 7 idle days, and the framework refuses any cadence that would fall back to directory listing.

slides.title: One framework, many sources
left: Full-load and change files to bronze and silver
Reload runbook rebuilds silver from bronze
right: lakeflow_connect adapter emits a managed pipeline
Same per-table config and data contract
Inherits tags, DQM, alerts and prerequisites
slides.notes: An adapter only describes what is specific to its source. Naming, tags, event logs, cadence, schemas, DQM and alerts are applied around it, and a test proves any new source type inherits them.
